designSummary: Registry-based cohort with matched population controls and infection controls; cause-specific Cox models split at one year.
sampleSize: 11,800 pneumonia survivors and about 47,200 population controls. Assuming about 1,400 first cardiovascular events among patients and 4,000 among controls in years two to five, the standard error of the log hazard ratio is about 0.031, so a hazard ratio of 1.3 would have a 95 percent confidence interval of about 1.22 to 1.38; precision rather than power limits interpretation, and the sample size is fixed by the registry.
primaryAnalysis: Cause-specific Cox models for the first cardiovascular event with death from other causes as a competing event, follow-up split at one year, adjusted for nine covariates fixed in advance: age, sex, deprivation quintile, frailty score, previous cardiovascular disease, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, chronic lung disease and smoking status from the registry.
secondaryAnalysis: The same models against infection controls; Fine-Gray models for absolute risk; all-cause death; care home entry among people living at home; a self-controlled case series for the first year as a sensitivity analysis.
missingData: Smoking status missing for about 8 percent is handled by multiple imputation with 20 imputations; people who leave the region are censored at the date of leaving.
multiplicity: One primary outcome in two windows against the population comparison; all other estimates are secondary and reported with confidence intervals.
software: R with the survival package; code and covariate list archived before linkage.
overfittingGuards: Complications of the index admission not adjusted for
Two comparison groups pre-specified, no others added
summary: Registry-sized cohort with precise estimates; Cox models split at one year against two comparison groups.
